findings.summary: DirStatCache::taint records lexical PathBuf ancestors, while lookup checks tainted.contains(dir) using the exact spelling. On Windows, case variants and 8.3 directory aliases resolve to the same directory but remain different cache keys. An independent probe cached AbsentDir through `...\newdirectory`, tainted and created `...\NewDirectory\victim.txt`, then still received Absent rather than Fallback through the equivalent spelling. A later chunk using an alternate parent spelling can therefore trust a stale absence while the earlier chunk writes, reopening the overwrite under --ignore-existing that cr-ls5-2 was intended to close.

The new release plan and release notes say non-UTF-8 filename failures are per-file-contained, but that is not true for remote transfers. The lossy manifest path makes tar-shard preparation fail at the source, and both the in-stream carrier (`source.prepare_payload(payload).await?`) and data-plane worker propagate that preparation error as a session failure. The release notes therefore promise that the remaining files proceed and exit 2 when a remote push can still abort wholesale.

Remote push with explicit `-p` but without `-v` loses the source-enumeration heartbeat introduced as a preserved fallback. The CLI creates a progress handle for `-p`, but run_remote_push constructs FsTransferSource with only execution.verbose and never attaches that handle to the source, so the source is both sinkless and non-verbose and the new gate suppresses its raw heartbeat. This contradicts the range's `(or -p)` documentation and can leave a slow remote enumeration silent until destination-side progress begins.
